question.problem: What is the last digit in the decimal expansion of ${12}^{17}?$
question.worked_solution:
If $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)$ and $c≡d\,(\text{mod}\,n),$ then the following properties hold:

- $ac≡bd\,(\text{mod}\,n)$

- ${a}^{k}≡{b}^{k}\,(\text{mod}\,n)$ for any positive integer $k$

To find the last digit, we need to calculate the following residue:

$$
{12}^{17}\text{ mod }10
$$

First, we note the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}12 & ≡10+2\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡0+2\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡2\, & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the exponentiation property, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{12}^{4} & ≡{2}^{4}\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡16\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡10+6\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡0+6\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡6\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\ {12}^{8} & ≡{6}^{2}\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡36\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡3\cdot 10+6\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡3\cdot 0+6\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡6\, & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we decompose ${12}^{17}$ into a product of smaller exponents. 

$$
{12}^{17}={({12}^{8})}^{2}\cdot 12
$$

By applying the multiplicative and exponentiation properties, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{12}^{17} & ≡{({12}^{8})}^{2}\cdot 12\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡(6)^{2}\cdot 2\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡36\cdot 2\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡72\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡7\cdot 10+2\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡7\cdot 0+2\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡2\, & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{12}^{17}\text{ mod }10=2
$$

which means that the last digit of ${12}^{17}$ is $2.$
